name: exascale.build
description: Agent-first, source-cited data layer for the US power system. Query operating, planned, and retired generation capacity (EIA-860M), net generation (EIA-923), and capacity factor — over MCP or REST. Every value returns with its source and as-of date, and any number resolves to its raw source cell with a matching SHA-256, so an agent's answer is verifiable in one call. Tools declare what they won't answer, so the agent refuses out-of-scope questions instead of guessing. Free and open today; industrial and logistics rolling out.

_published_faq.name: How do I add exascale.build to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add exascale.build to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.exascale.build/mcp.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the exascale.build MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: exascale.build provides these MCP tools: list_capabilities_v1, describe_power_capacity_v1, query_power_capacity_v1, describe_power_generation_v1, query_power_generation_v1, describe_capacity_factor_v1, query_capacity_factor_v1, and get_source_evidence_v1.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to exascale.build?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to exascale.build in data-analytics on the Manufact MCP catalog include Epicure, Newsflash, Point Topic, Pricing Optimizer AI, and StatCite.
exascale.build does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.
exascale.build is developed by Takezo. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
